characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester, load 9.8 N for 15 s
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 17Al alloy aged at 525 °C for 6 h has a Vickers hardness of 598.9 ± 10.4 HV (Table 3).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Each sample repeatedly tested 5 times; hardness given by the average of 5 measurements; specimens electrolytically polished in 10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the 17Al alloy after aging at 525 °C for 6 h

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV; main fields with 50 µm scale bars and higher-magnification insets (2 µm)
characterization_methods.key_findings: In the 525 °C – 6 h panel, a β-Mn grain-boundary feature is labelled (green) and an inset (2 µm) is labelled α-Mn (blue); at 525 °C β-Mn precipitation is sparse, occurring mostly along α grain boundaries with some short rod-shaped β-Mn within α grains.
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn and β-Mn) in the 17Al alloy after different aging treatments including 525 °C for 6 h

interfaces.phase_evolution: During aging at 525 °C the β-Mn precipitation in the 17Al alloy is kinetically slow: only a small amount of β-Mn forms (primarily along α grain boundaries plus a little short rod-shaped β-Mn within α grains), so the α matrix is not yet fully transformed at 6 h. Sequence followed: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: β-Mn precipitation kinetics at 525 °C aging (rate of α→β-Mn transformation)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting raw materials with high purity (>99.9 %) using a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
The ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h prior to hot rolling.
After homogenization, the ingots were hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm, then cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm3 samples by electrical discharge machining.
Samples were solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching.
Solution-treated samples were aged at 525 °C for 6 h, followed by water quenching. This is the terminal state of the sample.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester at a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the hardness is the average of 5 measurements. Samples prepared by electrolytic polishing in 10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol.

phases_present.morphology: primarily precipitated along α grain boundaries; a small amount of short rod-shaped β-Mn observed within the α grains
small particles in the α matrix

precipitates.distribution: along α grain boundaries (grain-boundary network) and short rod-shaped within α grains
small particles within the α matrix

structures.overall_structure: α (BCC) matrix of the 17Al alloy with only a small amount of β-Mn precipitated after aging at 525 °C for 6 h; the α matrix largely remains untransformed (β-Mn precipitation kinetics strongly slowed down at 525 °C).

unmapped_findings: Table 3: The solution-treated (parent) state of the 17Al alloy has a Vickers hardness of 259.8 ± 1.5 HV, a common baseline for all aging temperatures (b0030).

The 17Al alloy aged at 525 °C shows a monotonically increasing but slow hardening with time: 566.9 ± 9.7 HV (1 h), 585.0 ± 6.1 HV (3 h), 598.9 ± 10.4 HV (6 h) and 616.8 ± 12.3 HV (10 h) (b0030, Table 3).
At 525 °C the 17Al alloy fails to reach peak hardness within 10 h of aging; the optimal aging window for ultra-high hardness of the 17Al alloy is 550 °C–600 °C (b0038).
Composition of the 17Al alloy (EDS): Fe 43.2, Mn 34.8, Al 17.0, Cu 5.0 (at.%) and measured density 6.76 g·cm⁻³ (b0013, b0017).
